## Node Map

- The 3D map orbits continuously when the orbit icon beside the zoom controls is enabled. Mouse activity, editing and menus keep it running; toggle the icon off to stop. It stays still in 2D, hidden windows and reduced motion.
- The Node Map now shows every page of every workspace when it opens. Focusing on a workspace or a page's neighborhood keeps that group bright and dims the rest. The eye button (H) hides everything outside the focus, or shows only the workspaces when nothing is focused.
- Click a node to select it: its connections light up, the camera eases over and the details panel slides in with a preview, grouped connections and edit tools. Double-click or press Enter to dive into its neighborhood, and use the breadcrumb, Escape or Backspace to step back out. Arrow keys follow connections, O opens a page beside the map and Shift+O opens it in the main view. Hovering a node shows its kind, workspace and number of connections above node labels and map controls.
- Map controls are now compact icon buttons over the map: tools on the left, with undo and redo after an edit; layout, saved views, layers, zoom, fit, 3D/2D, show all and list view at the bottom right. Workspace chips focus a workspace, and Alt+click hides one. Chips that don't fit fold into a +N chip that lists the rest, and the focused workspace always stays on the bar. Search lights up matches in place and steps through them with Enter. The Layers panel can hide labels or connection types and doubles as the legend.
- Node Map shortcuts appear in Settings > Shortcuts and input and can be rebound. Show all, labels, hidden connection types, hidden workspaces and the details panel are remembered, and saved views remember the Show all setting.
- Switching between 3D and 2D is instant and no longer leaves the map stuck on the list view, because the map keeps one renderer for its whole life. Refreshing keeps the current map visible. If 3D rendering does stop, Try the map again brings it back. Connection lines use the theme's hairline strength.
- Large maps feel lighter. Moving the camera no longer recolors every node, hovering and selecting do less work, and refreshing an unchanged map redraws nothing. The Organic layout settles about five times faster on maps with thousands of pages.
- Nodes are colored by family and branch. Pages, databases, records and dashboards each keep their own color family, and every page tree gets its own shade within it, so related pages read as a group. The shades follow your theme and stay clear of neighboring families.
- Connection arrows have solid arrowheads that stay visible from any angle in 3D.
- In 3D, the map has depth from every angle. Workspaces spread evenly over a sphere instead of a flat ring, and each workspace's pages fill a sphere around it instead of a thin disc. Hierarchy levels become rings around each tree. 2D is unchanged. Pages also stay close to their parent page, or to their workspace if they're top level, so sparsely linked pages no longer drift off on their own.
- Explore all workspaces from the new Node Map in the sidebar or command palette. Expand a workspace, browse page hierarchy and references in 3D or 2D, search pages across workspaces, and open a page beside the map. A keyboard-friendly list provides the same navigation when 3D rendering is unavailable. Both map modes follow theme changes automatically, with stable analogous shades for pages, databases, records and dashboards. Palettes are cached between launches and refreshed when theme colors change. Records are optional, and large results show a notice instead of silently hiding pages.
- Switch to an organic link layout, group records by a chosen property, or explore a date timeline. Save named views, move and pin nodes, select a group with a box, and optionally follow the active page. Layout calculation runs separately from the editor, and motion follows your preferences.
- A live line follows your cursor while dragging a connection. Connect pages and records explicitly from the map: add references, change page nesting, or choose a relation property for task dependencies. Apply tags, status or date changes to selected pages or records. Map edits support undo and redo, reject cycles, and protect newer content from being overwritten. Changes save pending editor work first, and bulk changes apply together.

## Canvas, links and previews

- Workspace canvases fill the editor pane edge to edge, with a compact editable name over the board.
- Canvas text and page blocks stay sharp when zooming in.
- New Canvas view for databases: a freeform board where record cards, notes and images can be placed anywhere, resized and joined with labeled arrows. Zooming eases smoothly. Zoom with the scroll wheel, a trackpad pinch, or the zoom buttons; Shift+1 fits everything, Shift+2 zooms to the selection, and a minimap shows where you are. Hold Space or use the Hand tool (H) to pan, or Shift or Alt with the wheel for sideways or vertical movement; drag the background to select several items, then align, space them evenly, restack or duplicate them. Alignment guides help line items up, Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z undo and redo, and right-click opens a menu for items and the background. Double-click for a note, and paste or add images. Each canvas remembers where you left it, and duplicating a view copies its layout.
- New workspace canvases: make as many whiteboards as you like from the Canvases section in the sidebar, beside the page tree controls. Drag pages onto a canvas, or use Add page, to read and edit their full blocks directly. Page panels have editable titles, normal block tools and autosave; their bodies scroll and their headers move them. New panels start at a comfortable reading size. Notes, images and arrows still move, resize and connect, and removing a panel keeps its page. Canvases can be renamed, duplicated and deleted, and are included in workspace exports.
- Hovering an @mention or a link to another page shows a preview card with its title and opening lines, without leaving the page. Open it or open it beside the current page from the card.
- Type [[ to pick a page and link to it, the same way as @.
- Drag a page from the sidebar onto the text of another page to insert a link to it. Dragging several selected pages inserts all of them.
- The backlinks section is now "Linked to this page". It shows the whole paragraph around each link, with mentioned pages shown by title, and lists each table row that links to the page as "Column: value" pairs.

## Side-by-side work and planning

- Alt+click a page tab or drag it to the right edge to open it beside the current page. Resize the panes with the divider; notes, records, databases and dashboards can stay open together.
- Build a Master Calendar by connecting date properties from several project tables in Sources. Each source has its own color and visibility toggle.
- Day and Week calendars now have an Unscheduled Tasks drawer. Drag a task to a 15-minute time slot to set its source date, choose a block length, and undo scheduling from the notification.
- Drag the calendar handle on a board card or table record onto a Day or Week calendar to create a linked work session without changing its deadline. Clicking the handle opens the session editor.

## Editor and workflow

- Smart Paste turns a URL pasted over selected words into a link, hex colors into inline swatches, and GitHub issue links or absolute file paths into compact badges. Undo restores the previous content in one step; Paste as plain text skips conversion.
- The command palette can export the current page as PDF and create a task linked to a project, with saved destinations and task templates.
- Opening the command palette blocks scrolling and input on the page behind it, while search, commands and scrolling inside the palette remain available.
- Empty pages offer quiet shortcuts for block commands, adding a calendar, and picking a template. They disappear when you start writing. Page templates can be applied to the current empty page while keeping its title.
- Manual backups save pending edits from all open editors before creating the backup and prevent overlapping backup runs.

## Removed

- Removed the system-wide shortcuts for quick capture (Ctrl+Alt+N) and focusing Suivelle (Ctrl+Alt+S), including their Settings controls and the separate capture pop-up. Quick capture is still available inside Suivelle from the command palette and Ctrl+Shift+N.

## Maintenance

- Startup keeps the window responsive while checking and preparing the workspace. Loading screens show progress, and failed starts offer a retry instead of leaving a blank screen. The development launcher rebuilds outdated release executables.

- Updated CSV import code for compatibility with newer Rust toolchains.
- Promotional video project files are no longer tracked in the source repository.

## Documentation

- Updated the feature overview with mock screenshots of notes, project views, calendars, dashboards, and pages open beside one another.
- The demo now includes a studio calendar with sample events and tagged notes.
